# Intake Brief — Ensure all staff effects are implemented (MS-0MW4YAV24001Z7C6)

## Problem statement

Every staff card advertises an ability, and that ability is truthful only when it is backed by card data **and** applied by the engine. Nothing currently guarantees that pairing: the shipped `card-data.csv` compiles but an advertised effect can be description-only (a no-op). The audit performed for this intake inspected all 26 shipped staff templates plus the shipped pack staff and found **one** gap — the **Bookkeeper** advertises "Reduces this business ongoing cost by 20%" but has no backing card-data value, no parser support and no engine consumer, so the printed ability is not the ability the player gets. This item delivers the audit as a durable, reproducible artefact and creates a high-priority work item for every gap so none is silently lost.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — reads a staff card's printed ability and expects it to apply where the engine charges income, reputation, cost or incident damage.
- **Designer / balancer** — needs every staff ability backed by a `card-data.csv` value so economy tuning is trustworthy.
- **Developer / QA** — needs an authoritative audit trail and a regression guard so a missing effect fails the build instead of silently doing nothing.

### User stories

- As a player, I can trust that a staff card's printed ability is the ability I actually get.
- As a designer, every staff effect is backed by a data column/spec and a named engine consumer.
- As a developer, any staff effect that is not fully implemented is tracked as a high-priority work item, and the audit can be re-run when staff are added.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Full audit recorded.** Every shipped staff template (26 base in `src/card-data.csv` plus the shipped pack staff such as `stf-ms-residential-community-gardener`) is inspected and tabulated with: card id, advertised ability, backing card-data field/spec, engine consumer, and implemented/not status. The audit is stored durably (this work item's description and/or a `docs/game/` audit page) and is reviewable.
2. **Every gap has a high-priority work item.** Each staff effect found not fully implemented is captured as a high-priority work item with testable ACs. For the audit's single finding, the Bookkeeper gap is tracked as `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY`. No identified gap is left untracked.
3. **Audit is reproducible.** A documented procedure (or script) can re-run the audit against the current card data so future staff additions are checked the same way.
4. **Regression guard extended.** The staff cost-text/data consistency guard (`tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts`) is extended so a percentage-based staff cost-reduction description with no backing data fails the build (delivered with the Bookkeeper gap item, or here).
5. **Documentation updated.** The staff documentation (`docs/game/card-catalog.md`, and the audit page if added) reflects the audit and its findings. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A player can trust that every staff card's printed ability is real: the audit proves the roster is covered and the one broken ability (the Bookkeeper) is now captured as a high-priority, actionable work item instead of quietly misleading the player.

## Constraints

- **Audit only — no effect implementations here.** Effect fixes belong to the gap work items (e.g. `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY`). Keep this item's changes to the audit artefact, the gap-item creation and the guard/documentation.
- **Evidence-based.** Record a file:line or data-cell reference for each card's "implemented" verdict; a verdict without evidence is not accepted.
- **Do not rebalance** any coin/reputation value.
- **Minimal churn** — do not restructure the staff system.
- **Determinism** — no RNG changes.

### Out of scope

- Implementing the Bookkeeper effect (tracked in `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY`).
- Rebalancing staff costs/values.
- Broad refactors of the buff/ongoing-cost subsystems beyond what the audit and guard need.

## Existing state

The audit was performed during this intake by reading `src/card-data.csv`, the staff parsers (`MainStreetCardsTemplates.parseStaffEffect`), the buff/ongoing-cost helpers (`MainStreetStaffBuffs`) and their engine consumers. Result: **26/27 shipped staff are data-backed and engine-consumed; exactly one (Bookkeeper) is not.**

| Staff | Advertised ability | Backing data | Engine consumer | Status |
|-------|-------------------|--------------|-----------------|--------|
| `staff-assistant` | +2 hand slots | `handSlotsAdded=2` | `maxHandSize` (WeekStart / AiStrategy) | ✅ |
| `staff-manager` | +1 hand slot, +1 action | `handSlotsAdded=1`, `actionsPerTurn=1` | WeekStart / CompetitiveTurn | ✅ |
| `staff-director` | +3 hand slots, +1 action | `handSlotsAdded=3`, `actionsPerTurn=1` | WeekStart / CompetitiveTurn | ✅ |
| `staff-apprentice` | +1 hand slot | `handSlotsAdded=1` | `maxHandSize` | ✅ |
| `staff-executive` | +2 actions | `actionsPerTurn=2` | WeekStart / CompetitiveTurn | ✅ |
| `staff-socialite` | +1 hand slot, +10 rep/turn | `handSlotsAdded=1`, `reputationPerTurn=10` | `applyIncome` (AdjacencyScoring) | ✅ |
| `staff-accountant` | +1 hand slot, refresh −100, Tax 25% | `handSlotsAdded=1`, `refreshCostDiscount=100`, `taxAuditRate=0.25` | `refreshMarketCost`, `computeTaxAuditRate` | ✅ |
| `staff-general-manager` | +1 action, +4 hand slots | `actionsPerTurn=1`, `handSlotsAdded=4` | WeekStart / CompetitiveTurn | ✅ |
| `staff-lookout` | peek once/turn | `peekOncePerTurn=1` | `hasPeekCapableStaff` / EngineActions | ✅ |
| `staff-barista` | +20 coins each adjacent Food | `effect=income:adjacent:20:Food` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-security` | −10% incident coin (own+adjacent) | `effect=incident-coin:cluster:10` | `computeBusinessIncidentMitigation` | ✅ |
| `staff-marketing` | +10% reputation own business | `effect=reputation:percent:10` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-bookkeeper` | −20% ongoing cost own business | **none** | **none** | ❌ **GAP → `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY`** |
| `staff-customer-rep` | +10 rep each adjacent business | `effect=reputation:adjacent:10` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-it` | +1 synergy range | `effect=synergy-range:1` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-health-safety` | −10% incident frequency own | `effect=incident-frequency:own:10` | `computeIncidentFrequencyReduction` | ✅ |
| `staff-event-planner` | +100 coins each adjacent Entertainment | `effect=income:adjacent:100:Entertainment` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-delivery` | −50 adjacent purchases | `effect=purchase-discount:adjacent:50` | `computeAdjacentPurchaseDiscount` | ✅ |
| `staff-pr` | +15 rep own business | `effect=reputation:own:15` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-financial` | −100 upgrade cost own business | `upgradeCostDiscount=100` | `computeUpgradeCostDiscount` | ✅ |
| `staff-maintenance` | −50 incident rep (cluster) | `effect=incident-reputation:cluster:50` | `computeBusinessIncidentMitigation` | ✅ |
| `staff-investor` | free reroll/turn, 75% bias | `freeMarketRerollPerTurn=1`, `marketRelevanceBias=0.75` | `MainStreetMarketRefill` | ✅ |
| `staff-florist` | +30 coins adjacent Commerce/Culture | `effect=income:adjacent:30:Commerce\|Culture` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-baker` | +25 coins own business | `effect=income:own:25` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-chef` | +20% income own business | `effect=income:percent:20` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-mechanic` | +30 coins own business | `effect=income:own:30` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `stf-ms-residential-community-gardener` (pack) | +1 hand slot | `handSlotsAdded=1` | `maxHandSize` | ✅ |

Additional observations (not gaps): the Bookkeeper escapes the existing cost-text guard because `UNREGISTERED_COST_REDUCTION_RE` deliberately excludes percentage amounts; that guard hole is folded into the Bookkeeper gap item's AC4.

## Desired change

- Record the audit above as the durable artefact (this description and/or a `docs/game/staff-effect-audit.md` page).
- Add a short documented re-run procedure (a script or a checklist of the parser/buff/consumer files) so the audit is reproducible.
- Extend the staff cost-text guard to detect percentage-based ongoing-cost descriptions with no backing data (via the Bookkeeper gap item or here).
- Keep the Bookkeeper gap work item `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY` linked and high priority.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — link/append the audit reference so the roster points at the audit.
- `docs/game/staff-effect-audit.md` (new, optional) — the durable audit table + re-run procedure.
- `tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts` — percentage-aware guard (if delivered here).
- `src/card-data.csv` — read-only source of the audit (no changes here).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts`, `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — read-only consumers verified by the audit.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: the audit silently misses a gap** because a card's effect is partially wired (e.g. data exists but no consumer, or a consumer reads a different field). Mitigation: every "implemented" verdict cites both the data cell and the consumer symbol, and the guard/re-run procedure keeps it honest.
- **Risk: scope creep into implementation** — the audit item starts fixing effects instead of recording/tracking them. Mitigation: the audit item is explicitly audit + delegation; effect code belongs to gap items (e.g. `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY`).
- **Risk: future packs regress untracked.** Mitigation: the reproducible re-run procedure covers pack staff.
- **Assumption:** "all staff" = the shipped base roster plus shipped pack staff; dynamically authored future packs are covered by the re-run procedure.
- **Assumption:** this item is audit + delegation; the Bookkeeper fix is tracked in `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY`.
- **Assumption:** computing an effect's "implemented" status from data-cell + consumer-symbol evidence is sufficient (no runtime execution of every effect in this item).

## Related work

- **MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY** (open, high) — the single gap this audit found: Bookkeeper −20% ongoing-cost effect not implemented (`discovered-from:` this item).
- **MS-0MW3JXF6U00753LB** (completed) — two-type staff redesign that wired the per-business `effect` specs and their consumers; left the Bookkeeper without a spec.
- **MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M** (completed) — precedent for backfilling a description-only staff effect end-to-end with a guard.
- **MS-0MULWBSF9000Z64Z** (completed) — staff description ×100 consistency; created the guard extended here.
- **MS-0MW2XKTR50062OFL** (completed) — GDD staff consistency verification (a sibling consistency-check pattern to mirror for reproducibility).
- **CG-0MT4WXNR80090FXZ** — specialization applicant wave that introduced the Bookkeeper.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No blocking questions. The seed context ("iterate over all staff, inspect the code, create high-priority work items for gaps") fully defines the audit deliverable, and the repo provided all evidence needed. **Assumption recorded:** this item is an *audit + delegation* task — effect fixes live in the gap work items (the Bookkeeper fix is `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY`), not in this item. **Assumption recorded:** "all staff" means the shipped base roster plus shipped pack staff; dynamically authored future packs are covered by the reproducible re-run procedure rather than individually audited here.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY** – Bookkeeper -20% ongoing-cost staff effect is not implemented (open)
- **MS-0MW6HEBP80070YND** – Staff effects are not implemented (open)
- **MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M** – Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects (completed)

# Clicking to close the end-of-turn ledger selects the card below

## Problem statement

Pressing an action button on the end-of-turn ledger (the **Turn Summary** dialog — `[ Next Turn ]`, and by extension `[ Bank Loan ]`) also selects the hand card rendered underneath it. Closing the ledger should only resume the deferred closing; it must leave the hand untouched.

## Users

- **The human player, at the end of every day** — has just reviewed their P&L statement and presses `[ Next Turn ]` to start the next day.
  - *As a player closing the end-of-turn ledger, I want the hand to be exactly as I left it, so that I do not start the next day with an accidental card selection or an unexpected "placing from hand" state.*
- **A player who ends the day with a full hand** — the hand row is directly under the ledger's action row, so this is the common case, not an edge case.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Pressing `[ Next Turn ]` on the Turn Summary dialog dismisses the ledger and starts the next day **without** selecting, highlighting, or entering a "placing from hand" / "event selected" state for any hand card (`pendingHandIndex` stays `null`, `uiPhase` returns to `market`, and no card is bought, moved, played, or discarded).
- Pressing `[ Bank Loan ]` (enabled) opens the mid-game loan selector and likewise never changes hand-card selection; cancelling back to the summary leaves the hand untouched.
- The fix holds when the ledger's action button geometrically overlaps a hand card (the normal layout: the middle hand card sits directly under `[ Next Turn ]`), and for both mouse and touch input.
- A regression test reproduces the defect in a real Phaser scene: it positions a hand card under the ledger's action button, dispatches a real pointer press/release at the button, asserts the closing resumes (or the loan selector opens) **and** asserts the hand-card selection state is unchanged.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Closing the end-of-turn ledger no longer selects a hand card, so every new day starts with a clean hand and no accidental placement state.

## Constraints

- The Turn Summary dialog is the only gate in front of the deferred closing: `[ Next Turn ]` must remain the sole way to resume it, and the enabled/disabled `[ Bank Loan ]` matrix, tab switching and keyboard navigation must keep working exactly as today.
- Overlay-pattern compliance (AGENTS.md UI best practices): `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` from `@ui`, all elements parented into `s.hudContainer`, depths 199 (backdrop) / 200 (box) / 201 (elements), everything tracked in `s.overlayObjects`, instant appearance (no fade — reduced-motion safe).
- The fix must not weaken the deliberate click-through protections elsewhere (tutorial tooltip DOMElement isolation, `CG-0MSTB03U6009J2WV`) or the drag-drop click-vs-drag thresholds.
- No new engine/state semantics: this is a presentation/input bug; the closing economy and ledger figures must be untouched.
- Reduced-motion, replay/headless and competitive paths must keep their current pacing and behaviour.

## Existing state

- The Turn Summary dialog is rendered by `presentTurnSummaryPanel()` in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts`. The panel is `PANEL_WIDTH = 680` × `PANEL_HEIGHT = 640`, centred on the 1280×720 scene (`panelY ≈ 40`, bottom ≈ 680).
- Its action row sits at `btnY = panelY + PANEL_H - 62 ≈ 618`, with `[ Next Turn ]` at `centerX - 120 ≈ (520, 618)` and `[ Bank Loan ]` at `centerX + 120 ≈ (760, 618)`.
- The hand row is centred on `columnCenterX ≈ 467` with `handY ≈ 628` and `handCardH = 80`, so hand cards span roughly y 590–666 and x 251–683 (three 140 px cards at ≈ 319 / 467 / 615). **`[ Next Turn ]` therefore sits directly over the middle hand card.**
- The action buttons act on `pointerdown` (`nextTurnBtn.on('pointerdown', …)` → `dismissPanel()` then `handlers.onNextTurn()`). The hand's business/upgrade cards act on `pointerup` in the drag-drop path (`container.on('pointerup', …)` → `onHandBusinessCardClick` / `onHandUpgradeCardClick`), and the closing's `advanceTurn` starts the next day only after a bounded wait (`s.time.delayedCall(800, …)` or the bounded income-collection deferral).
- Working hypothesis to confirm during implementation: the button's `pointerdown` destroys the button and the full-screen input-blocking backdrop, so the matching `pointerup` hit-tests against the now-uncovered hand card beneath and its click-to-select handler fires. Because the button overlaps the card, this is repeatable for the common full-hand case.
- Related work already shipped: the tabbed P&L Turn Summary (`MS-0MW4XULA90002OEY`), the turn-summary gate (`MS-0MVP46Q8X003419R`), the bank-loan button (`MS-0MVXYCICT0051LU7`), and the tutorial tooltip click-through fix (`CG-0MSTB03U6009J2WV`).

## Desired change

- Make the ledger's action buttons consume the complete press/release cycle so a `[ Next Turn ]` / `[ Bank Loan ]` press can never be interpreted as a hand-card click, even when the button overlaps the hand row.
- Alternatively (or additionally), ensure the hand layer cannot receive pointer events while the Turn Summary overlay is presented — without blocking the overlay's own controls.
- Keep the ledger's layout, values, tab strip, keyboard navigation and the `[ Next Turn ]`-only resume contract unchanged.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the reported control is `[ Next Turn ]` in the Turn Summary dialog (the "end-of-turn ledger"); the same renderer serves the competitive panel, so the fix must cover both.
- **Risk — over-blocking:** a blunt "disable the hand layer while any overlay is up" change could break legitimate hand interactions after dismissal, or the drag-drop manager's registered draggables. Prefer a scoped guard that only suppresses hand clicks during the ledger's own press, and restore it on dismissal.
- **Risk — button responsiveness:** moving the action buttons from `pointerdown` to `pointerup` would change the press feel and could interact with the drag thresholds; if chosen, cover it with the existing dialog browser tests.
- **Risk — layout regression:** shrinking or moving the panel to avoid the hand row must keep every statement line, the tab strip and the `[ Bank Loan ]` hint on-screen at 1280×720 (and the reduced-motion/instant-appearance contract).
- **Scope-creep guard:** anything beyond "the ledger's action must not select a hand card" (e.g. a general overlay-input audit, or tooltip behaviour in the ledger — `MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO`) is a separate work item, not this fix.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts` — the dialog renderer: action buttons (`[ Next Turn ]`, `[ Bank Loan ]`), dismissal, overlay objects; the primary fix site.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `presentTurnSummaryGate()` / `advanceTurn()` / `finishTurnPresentation()`; the closing that the button resumes.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — hand-card `pointerup` click handlers (`onHandBusinessCardClick` / `onHandUpgradeCardClick`) and the drag-drop registration; the leaked event's destination.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — `onHandBusinessCardClick` / `onHandUpgradeCardClick` / `onHandEventCardClick` and their `uiPhase` gates.
- `core/src/ui/Overlay.ts` / `core/src/ui/OverlayButton.ts` — shared backdrop/button factories and their input behaviour.
- `core/src/ui/HandView.ts` — hand layout (card positions) and interactive card sprites.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` — existing overlay browser coverage to extend.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-gate.test.ts` — existing gate coverage.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — Turn Summary dialog + closing gate documentation (update the interaction contract).

## Related work

- `MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41` — End of Turn summary dialog (parent epic; completed).
- `MS-0MW4XULA90002OEY` — Turn summary as a P&L statement (completed).
- `MS-0MVP46Q8X003419R` — Turn Summary gate (completed).
- `MS-0MVXYCICT0051LU7` / `MS-0MVXYCJCK006UE62` — Bank Loan button and its enabled/disabled matrix (completed).
- `MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ` — Refactor end-of-turn presentation (completed).
- `MS-0MV767QTO008JUDJ` — Clicking a selected hand card deselects it (completed; same selection state).
- `MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO` — Tooltips in the end-of-turn ledger (open; same dialog).
- `CG-0MSTB03U6009J2WV` — Tutorial tooltip pointer pass-through fix (completed; same class of click-through defect).
- Repository docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (Turn Summary dialog + closing gate), `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were needed. The seed report ("When I click on the button to close the end of turn ledger, the card in my hand below the button is selected. It should not be.") identifies the dialog (the Turn Summary / end-of-turn ledger), the trigger (its action button) and the defect (hand-card selection) unambiguously, and repo research resolved the rest.
- Q: "Which control is 'the button to close the end of turn ledger'?" — Answer (agent research): the `[ Next Turn ]` button in the Turn Summary dialog (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts`). Evidence: `MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO` uses "end-of-turn ledger" to mean the Turn Summary dialog; the dialog's only close/resume control is `[ Next Turn ]`.
- Q: "Is the defect a layout overlap or an input-handling leak?" — Answer (agent research, to be confirmed during implementation): both are present — the action row geometrically overlaps the middle hand card, and the button dismisses the overlay on `pointerdown` so the matching `pointerup` can reach the hand card. Evidence: computed panel/hand geometry and the `pointerdown` / `pointerup` handlers above.
- Assumption (documented): the primary target is single-player play; the competitive per-seat panel uses the same renderer and `[ Next Turn ]` button, so the fix should cover it too.

# Intake brief — Cards should represent the actual income and reputation changes

## Problem statement

During play, the income and reputation figures shown on a placed business or community-space card are derived from the card's static values plus any upgrade bonus (`baseIncome + incomeBonus` and `reputationPerTurn + reputationBonus`). They ignore the modifiers the engine actually credits — board synergy, the same-type adjacency penalty, the duplicate-business (market-saturation) factor, and staff bonuses. A card can therefore display `+161` while the player is credited a different amount, so the card text contradicts the game economy and misleads placement and staffing decisions.

## Users

- **Players** who plan placements, upgrades and staff hires from the numbers shown on their cards.
  - "As a player, I want a placed card's text to show the income and reputation it actually generates, so I can make placement and staffing decisions without guessing."
  - "As a player, when I place a synergy neighbour or employ a Chef, I want the card's numbers to update immediately, so I can see the effect of my decision."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Placed business/community-space cards show the **effective per-turn income** (base + upgrade bonus + synergy + duplicate factor + staff bonuses) in the on-card cash line, equal to the per-slot amount the engine credits.
- Placed cards show the **effective per-turn reputation** (base + upgrade bonus + synergy) in the on-card reputation text, equal to the engine's per-slot reputation credit.
- Hover tooltips for placed street cards, hand cards and market cards report the same effective income/reputation values as the on-card text, so no display surface shows stale base-only figures for a placed card.
- Unplaced cards (hand/market) continue to show their unmodified base + upgrade values, because board and staff effects do not apply until placement.
- Staff bonuses are folded into the displayed values on demand (read-only) without mutating the `currentIncome` / `currentReputationPerTurn` caches, reusing the same computation path as `applyIncome` so the displayed text can never disagree with the credited amount.
- Tests cover a plain card, a card with a synergy neighbour, a card with an employed staff bonus (own and adjacent), and a duplicate-saturated card, asserting the displayed values equal the engine's per-slot credited amounts across the overlay and tooltip paths.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players will be able to trust the income and reputation numbers on their cards: the text will match the coins and reputation actually credited each turn, so placement and staffing decisions are informed by real values rather than static base figures.

## Constraints

- The adjacency caches (`currentIncome`, `currentReputationPerTurn`) are read-only during display; staff buffs must be recomputed on demand, per the caching-safety contract documented in `MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`.
- Display computation must share the engine's source of truth (`computeBusinessIncome`, `computeBusinessStaffBuffs`, `computePerBusinessSkillBuffs`) so display and credit can never diverge.
- Rendering runs per card per refresh, so avoid expensive recomputation beyond what the engine already does each turn; memoise or cache per-slot effective values if needed.
- Baked SVG card faces (`generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` and the static assets) currently show no income/reputation text; the fix is in the Phaser overlay/tooltip layer, not the SVG faces.
- Reduced-motion, replay and headless modes must remain visually and behaviourally unchanged.

## Existing state

- **On-card income/reputation:** `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec()` (`src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts`) computes `totalIncome = baseIncome + incomeBonus` and `totalReputation = reputationPerTurn + reputationBonus`. These are rendered by `applyUpgradeOverlays()` on street, hand and market cards.
- **Street hover tooltip:** built inline in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` as `Income: +${baseIncome + incomeBonus}/turn`, with reputation from `reputationPerTurn + reputationBonus`.
- **Hand/market hover tooltip:** `buildCardTooltipInfo()` in `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` uses the same base + bonus formula.
- **Actual values:** `card.currentIncome` = base + upgrade + synergy + duplicate factor (set by `syncCardCurrentIncome` / `recalculateCard` in `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`); `card.currentReputationPerTurn` = base reputation + upgrade bonus + synergy reputation. Staff buffs are deliberately **not** cached and are applied read-only in `applyIncome()` via `computeBusinessStaffBuffs()` and `computePerBusinessSkillBuffs()`.
- `generateBusinessCardSvg()` also uses base + bonus but is test-only (not on the production render path).

## Desired change

Make every card display surface show the values the engine actually credits for a placed card, with staff bonuses included on demand, while keeping unplaced cards on their base + upgrade values and leaving the adjacency caches untouched.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — accept/extract effective income and reputation (needs grid/staff context or precomputed per-slot values).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — pass per-slot effective values into the overlay spec and update the street tooltip text.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — `buildCardTooltipInfo()` (and any street tooltip builder) use effective values for placed cards.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — expose a read-only per-slot effective income/reputation helper reusing `computeBusinessIncome`, `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` and `computePerBusinessSkillBuffs`.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — existing staff buff helpers (consumed read-only; never mutated).
- `src/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `getIncomeResult()` preview path, if it should also agree with the effective values.
- `tests/main-street/` — new/updated tests asserting displayed values equal the engine's per-slot credited amounts.

## Related work

- **MS-0MV8LHN0W0017XU1** – Reputation bonuses should have no delay between businesses (completed).
- **MS-0MVRDGNFU001DDQW** – Park should give a good reputation bonus (completed).
- **MS-0MUVB2ZES005V83Y** – AI should not use Community Favour as much (completed).
- **MS-0MW0UCMF9004H9NT** – Single-player income: duplicate-factor applied to `computeBusinessIncome` / `syncCardCurrentIncome` (completed) — establishes the cached `currentIncome` values this item should display.
- **MS-0MVYG50V1007W8BP** – Reduced income for duplicate businesses (completed) — the duplicate-factor link surface.
